mechanism_narrative: A quarterly increase in GDP (GDPC1) exceeding 2% signals strengthening economic growth, leading to positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX produces negative 60-day returns in > 50% of quarters with GDPC1 growth > 2%.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained federal funds rate (FEDFUNDS) below 1% indicates accommodative monetary policy, driving positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: Walk-forward Rank IC remains below 0.02 over any 1.5-year rolling window.

mechanism_narrative: When unemployment (UNRATE) falls below 4% and payroll employment (PAYEMS) grows by more than 200,000 in a month, the combined labor market strength predicts positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 5 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX returns are negative in > 60% of triggered instances.

mechanism_narrative: Industrial production (INDPRO) growth exceeding 1.5% month-over-month signals supply chain resilience, leading to positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: Walk-forward correlation between INDPRO growth and SPX returns is not significantly positive (p > 0.10).

mechanism_narrative: Housing starts (HOUST) increasing by more than 10% year-over-year, combined with rising retail sales (RSAFS), predict positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days due to broadening demand.
candidate_trigger: HOUST YoY change > 10% and RSAFS monthly change > 0
failure_condition: SPX returns are not significantly higher in triggered quarters compared to non-triggered (t-test p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A decrease in the federal funds rate (FEDFUNDS) by more than 50 basis points within a quarter signals a pivot towards monetary easing, leading to positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: Walk-forward analysis shows no significant difference in SPX returns between easing and non-easing quarters (p > 0.10).

mechanism_narrative: Always-on: the labor market's influence on consumer spending ensures that payroll employment (PAYEMS) growth is positively correlated with S&P 500 forward returns over the next 5 trading days.
failure_condition: Walk-forward correlation analysis reveals a non-positive correlation between PAYEMS growth and SPX returns (p < 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: Regime-conditional: in a post-shock recovery regime, a monthly increase in retail sales (RSAFS) by more than 1% predicts positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days as demand recovers.
failure_condition: In post-shock recovery regimes, SPX returns are not significantly higher when RSAFS growth exceeds 1% compared to when it does not (t-test p > 0.05).
